items.title: Winners and losers of the LeBron James 'last decision'
items.summary: The content-creating world’s long international nightmare is over: LeBron James has chosen his new team. And, in a move that will bring no small consternation to fans in Northeast Ohio and Biscayne Bay, he has indeed chosen a new team.The leading scorer in NBA history is now a member of the Philadelphia 76ers, agreeing to terms on a two-year, $8 million contract to line up alongside Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, fellow new arrival Jaylen Brown and rising sophomore VJ Edgecombe in the City of Brotherly Love. (What percentage of the Sixers’ salary cap figure will James account for? Just over 2.3%, for No. 23. There are no coincidences.)The reverberations from this one will be felt far and wide; let’s start getting our arms around it all.What follows is a stab at a first draft of history — a thumbnail sketch of who and what seems to have been helped and hurt by Friday’s blockbuster…

items.title: LeBron James' deal with the 76ers is a high school reunion with president of basketball operations Mike Gansey
items.summary: LeBron James' decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76erswill come with plenty of ripple effects. One of them is a full circle moment involving the man he just handed a major win.The 41-year-old James will be reuniting with Mike Gansey, the 43-year-old president of basketball operations in Philadelphia. items.summary: Philadelphia was always on the list of teams LeBron James was seriously considering, but talking to executives and others at NBA Summer League and after, the 76ers were usually dismissed. They were fourth or fifth on people's lists. Great basketball fit, but was LeBron really going to end his career 2,700 miles away from his family, playing for a team he had never played for before?Yes, he is.LeBron James is joining the Philadelphia 76ers on a two-year deal (at the veteran minimum, with a player option on the second year). Who were the winners and losers from this decision? Let's break it all down.Winner: Philadelphia 76ersPhiladelphia was swept out of the playoffs last May by the Knicks, and it was hard to envision a path forward. items.summary: LeBron James knew Mike Gansey before he signed with the Philadelphia 76ers in NBA free agency. The NBA's all-time leading scorer and the 76ers' new president of basketball operations go back decades — all the way back to their high school days in Northeast Ohio, when James and the future West Virginia standout initially emerged as regional basketball stars. items.summary: At long last, LeBron James has made his decision. The 41-year-old is a Sixer, signing a two-year deal worth $8 million to join Philadelphia.Is Bronny James next? For James' free agency, it's not clear what the exact terms of engagement were during this round. But unlike past courtships, the employment status of James' son, Bronny, will likely be part of internal discussions with LeBron's new team in Philly. In 2024, when James' Los Angeles Lakers selected Bronny with the 55th pick in the draft, the Jameses became the first father-son pairing to play in the NBA together. LeBron has not publicly stated that he'd like his eldest son to join him, and it's not a given the Lakers would satisfy any such request.
